```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 6, dpi = 500, fig.retina = 1, crop = FALSE, dev = "png", dev.args = list(type = "cairo"), out.width = "100%", fig.align = "center")
library(GeneTrackR)
library(patchwork)
plain_text <- ggplot2::element_text(family = "Arial", colour = "black", face = "plain")
tutorial_text <- ggplot2::theme(text = plain_text, axis.text = plain_text,
  axis.title = plain_text, plot.title = plain_text, plot.subtitle = plain_text,
  plot.caption = plain_text, legend.text = plain_text, legend.title = plain_text,
  strip.text = plain_text)
classic_style <- ggplot2::theme_classic(base_family = "Arial") + tutorial_text
ggplot2::theme_set(classic_style)
demo_file <- function(name) system.file("extdata", name, package = "GeneTrackR", mustWork = TRUE)
```

# Introduction

This workflow exports standard genomic tracks for downstream software and
retains structured R results for reproducibility. It uses the same synthetic
inputs as the [complete workflow](complete-workflow.html), with no external
downloads or persistent user-file overwrites. Package website:
<https://renscq.github.io/GeneTrackR/>.

# Prepare inputs and a temporary output directory

```{r inputs}
input_files <- c(annotation = demo_file("gtr_demo.genePredExt"),
  variants = demo_file("gtr_demo_variants.vcf"),
  phenotype = demo_file("gtr_demo_pheno.tsv"),
  signal = demo_file("gtr_demo_rnaseq_plus.bedgraph"))
stopifnot(length(input_files) == 4L, all(file.exists(input_files)))
gp <- read_genepred(input_files[["annotation"]], format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
vcf <- read_vcf(input_files[["variants"]], mode = "memory",
  verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
pheno <- read_pheno(input_files[["phenotype"]], verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
signal <- read_bwg(input_files[["signal"]],
  sample_names = "RNA_seq_plus", strand = "+", mode = "memory", verbose = FALSE)
hap <- hap_gene_variant(vcf, annotation = gp, gene_id = "GeneA", genotype_mode = "string")
association <- plot_hap_pheno(hap, phenotype = pheno, traits = "protein_content",
  min_hap_samples = 3, test_method = "t.test", p_adjust = "BH",
  p_value_type = "adjusted", text_size = 10)
association$figure <- association$figure & classic_style
output_dir <- tempfile("GeneTrackR-export-")
dir.create(output_dir)
```

For a production analysis, choose a deliberate output directory and keep input
files immutable. Record assembly, coordinate convention, signal units and
normalization, sample inclusion and all analysis parameters alongside outputs.

# Standard-format tracks

## Annotation

```{r annotation-output}
annotation_file <- file.path(output_dir, "annotation.genePredExt")
write_feature(gp, file = annotation_file, format = "genepredext", overwrite = TRUE)
write_feature(gp, file = file.path(output_dir, "annotation.bed12"),
  format = "bed12", overwrite = TRUE)
restored_annotation <- read_genepred(annotation_file, format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(restored_annotation$genes) == 20L,
  nrow(restored_annotation$transcripts) == 24L)
```

Writers apply the target-format coordinate convention. GTF/GFF3, BED and
GenePred represent different attributes and hierarchy information, so a
standard-format export should not be treated as a lossless copy of an entire
R workflow object. Use the function reference for supported formats and their
attribute/identifier policies; retain an RDS object when all metadata matter.

## Signal and VCF

```{r signal-and-variant-output}
signal_files <- write_bwg(signal, outdir = output_dir, format = "bedgraph", overwrite = TRUE)
variant_file <- file.path(output_dir, "variants.vcf")
write_vcf(vcf, file = variant_file, overwrite = TRUE)
restored_variants <- read_vcf(variant_file, mode = "memory", verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(restored_variants$data) == nrow(vcf$data),
  identical(restored_variants$meta$sample_names, character()))
stopifnot(file.copy(input_files[["variants"]], file.path(output_dir, "original-genotypes.vcf")))
signal_files
```

Signal export supports the existing bedGraph/WIG/BigWig layer. Consult
`?write_bwg` for chromosome-size and sample-splitting requirements, especially
for BigWig. Raw and normalized values are distinct outputs and should be
labelled with units and normalization parameters.

**Current VCF writer limitation:** `write_vcf()` and its compatibility wrapper
write the eight core site fields only. They omit FORMAT and sample genotype
columns and write a minimal metadata header. The read-back assertion above
therefore checks a sites-only export, not a genotype-preserving round trip.
Keep the original VCF/header and complete RDS when genotypes or typed metadata
are required; the example copies the unchanged original file separately.
Genotype-preserving VCF export and standard-VCF interchange remain future work.
The [class/I/O rationale](annotation.html#design-decisions) describes that boundary.

# Save statistical tables, figures and complete objects

```{r analysis-output}
utils::write.csv(as.data.frame(association$summary),
  file.path(output_dir, "phenotype-summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
utils::write.csv(as.data.frame(association$pvalue),
  file.path(output_dir, "pairwise-tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "phenotype-comparison.png"),
  plot = association$figure, width = 8, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 500,
  device = grDevices::png, type = "cairo")
bundle <- list(annotation = gp, variants = vcf, signal = signal,
  haplotypes = hap, phenotype = pheno, association = association,
  parameters = list(gene_id = "GeneA", genotype_mode = "string", min_hap_samples = 3,
    trait = "protein_content", test_method = "t.test", p_adjust = "BH"))
saveRDS(bundle, file.path(output_dir, "analysis.rds"))
restored <- readRDS(file.path(output_dir, "analysis.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(restored$variants$meta$sample_names, vcf$meta$sample_names),
  identical(restored$haplotypes$haplotypes$sample_n, hap$haplotypes$sample_n))
```

`plot_hap_variant()` and integrated-track functions return figures directly.
Phenotype and variant-effect functions return tables plus `$figure`;
`plot_ld_block()` normally returns LDTrack with `$figure`. Select the figure
component explicitly when calling `ggsave()`.

Report sample sizes, trait units, effect direction, adjustment method and
appropriate uncertainty, not only P values or significance symbols. For the
example's single trait, the six pairwise Welch t-tests use BH adjustment.
The complete object preserves interpretation context that is lost in a CSV
or image alone.

# Browser use and provenance {#browser-export}

For real IGV/UCSC-style browser inspection, use a reference/assembly matching
the exported coordinates and chromosome names. The demo coordinates describe
a synthetic model and are not a claim about a real reference genome. Load
annotation, signal and VCF tracks at the same interval and check strand,
sample labels and y-axis scale before comparing views.

GeneTrackR's integrated browser-like plot is generated in R, as demonstrated
in the [complete workflow](complete-workflow.html#integrated-browser). External
browser applications and network services are not required to execute these
vignettes.

```{r provenance}
provenance <- data.frame(role = names(input_files), input = basename(input_files),
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_files)))
stopifnot(nrow(provenance) == 4L, !anyNA(provenance$md5), all(nchar(provenance$md5) == 32L))
utils::write.csv(provenance, file.path(output_dir, "input-checksums.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(output_dir, "session-info.txt"))
list.files(output_dir)
```

Before sharing results, verify record counts, sample/ID alignment, missing
values, coordinate conventions, fields required by the target format and
read-back results. Keep original inputs and complete R objects. The
[annotation workflow](annotation.html) checks that direct transcript-level
CDS summaries match explicit segment aggregation, with one observation per
transcript and feature.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
